description: Question bank on Social and Cultural History of Karnataka - Religion and Philosophy, derived from FDA & SDA exam-oriented notes. Covers Vachana movement, Lingayat movement, Haridasa movement, saints, philosophical traditions, Jainism, Buddhism, Sufism, Islam, Christianity, folk religion and pilgrimage centres.

questions.subject: Karnataka History
questions.question: What is meant by religion?

options.A: A system of beliefs, worship, ethical values, rituals and practices through which individuals and communities understand the sacred and their relationship with it
options.B: The systematic examination of fundamental questions about reality, knowledge, consciousness, ethics, God and liberation
options.C: A political ideology governing state administration
options.D: A form of economic organisation based on trade

questions.explanation: Religion is a system of beliefs, worship, ethical values, rituals and practices through which individuals and communities understand the sacred and their relationship with it.

questions.subject: Karnataka History
questions.question: What is meant by philosophy?

options.A: A system of beliefs and rituals centred on the sacred
options.B: The systematic examination of fundamental questions about reality, knowledge, consciousness, ethics, God and liberation
options.C: The study of ancient inscriptions and monuments
options.D: The practice of devotional singing in temples

questions.explanation: Philosophy is the systematic examination of fundamental questions about reality, knowledge, consciousness, ethics, God and liberation.

questions.subject: Karnataka History
questions.question: Why is Karnataka important in the religious history of India?

options.A: It was the only region where Buddhism flourished
options.B: It has been a major centre for Jainism, Buddhism, Shaivism, Vaishnavism, Lingayat traditions, Hindu philosophical schools, Sufi traditions, Islam, Christianity and diverse local folk religions
options.C: It was the birthplace of Adi Shankaracharya
options.D: It was the centre of the Mughal Empire

questions.explanation: Karnataka has been a major centre for Jainism, Buddhism, Shaivism, Vaishnavism, Lingayat traditions, Hindu philosophical schools, Sufi traditions, Islam, Christianity and diverse local folk religions.

questions.subject: Karnataka History
questions.question: Which factors helped different religious traditions flourish in Karnataka?

options.A: Only royal patronage
options.C: Royal patronage, trade routes, monasteries and maths, pilgrimage centres, local devotional movements, literary activity and interaction among communities

questions.explanation: Royal patronage, trade routes, monasteries and maths, pilgrimage centres, local devotional movements, literary activity and interaction among communities helped different religious traditions flourish in Karnataka.

questions.subject: Karnataka History
questions.question: What is Bhakti?

options.A: The performance of elaborate Vedic sacrifices
options.B: Loving devotion or personal commitment to a deity, expressed through prayer, song, service, remembrance and surrender
options.C: The study of ancient philosophical texts
options.D: The practice of severe physical austerities

questions.explanation: Bhakti is loving devotion or personal commitment to a deity, expressed through prayer, song, service, remembrance and surrender.

questions.subject: Karnataka History
questions.question: What is Moksha or Mukti?

options.A: The attainment of worldly wealth
options.B: Liberation from the cycle of birth and death (samsara)

questions.explanation: Moksha or Mukti means liberation from the cycle of birth and death (samsara), though different philosophical traditions explain its nature differently.

questions.subject: Karnataka History
questions.question: What is Dharma?

options.A: Duty, moral order, righteous conduct and the principles that sustain individual and social life
options.B: The cycle of birth and death
options.C: The performance of music and dance
options.D: The worship of a personal deity

questions.explanation: Dharma refers to duty, moral order, righteous conduct and the principles that sustain individual and social life; it means various by context and tradition.

questions.subject: Karnataka History
questions.question: What is the difference between a religious movement and a philosophical school?

options.A: A religious movement is more systematic than a philosophical school
options.B: A religious movement is a social and devotional current involving communities and practices, while a philosophical school presents a more systematic account of reality, knowledge and liberation
options.C: A philosophical school involves communities, while a religious movement is purely theoretical
options.D: There is no difference between the two

questions.explanation: A religious movement is a social and devotional current involving communities and practices, while a philosophical school presents a more systematic account of reality, knowledge and liberation; a movement may contain several philosophical interpretations.

questions.subject: Karnataka History
questions.question: What was the Vachana movement?

options.A: A 12th-century Kannada devotional, spiritual and social reform movement led by Basavanna and other Sharanas in the Kalyana region
options.C: A 13th-century philosophical school founded by Madhvacharya

questions.explanation: The Vachana movement was a major 12th-century Kannada devotional, spiritual and social reform movement led by Basavanna and other Sharanas in the Kalyana region.

questions.subject: Karnataka History
questions.question: When did the Vachana movement flourish?

options.A: 8th century CE

questions.explanation: The Vachana movement flourished mainly during the 12th century CE.

questions.subject: Karnataka History
questions.question: Where was the Vachana movement centred?

options.A: Udupi
options.B: Kalyana, present-day Basavakalyan in Bidar district

questions.explanation: Kalyana, present-day Basavakalyan in Bidar district, Karnataka, was its principal historical centre.

questions.subject: Karnataka History
questions.question: Who was the leading figure of the Vachana movement?

options.A: Allama Prabhu

questions.explanation: Basavanna, also known as Basaveshwara, was the leading figure of the Vachana movement.

questions.subject: Karnataka History
questions.question: What were Vachanas?

options.A: Long epic poems in Sanskrit
options.B: Short Kannada devotional and philosophical utterances, generally written in a direct prose-poetic style and often ending with a personal divine signature (ankita)

questions.explanation: Vachanas were short Kannada devotional and philosophical utterances, generally written in a direct prose-poetic style and often ending with a personal divine signature (ankita).

questions.subject: Karnataka History
questions.question: What language did the Vachanakaras use?

options.A: Sanskrit
options.C: Kannada, often in an accessible form that communicated spiritual and ethical ideas beyond the learned elite

questions.explanation: The Vachanakaras used Kannada, often in an accessible form that communicated spiritual and ethical ideas beyond the learned elite.

questions.subject: Karnataka History
questions.question: What were the major aims of the Vachana movement?

options.A: To promote personal devotion to Shiva, ethical conduct, dignity of labour, social equality, sharing, and criticism of empty ritual and social discrimination
options.B: To establish a new empire in Karnataka
options.C: To spread Buddhism across South India
options.D: To promote Sanskrit as the sole language of worship

questions.explanation: The major aims of the Vachana movement were to promote personal devotion to Shiva, ethical conduct, dignity of labour, social equality, sharing, and criticism of empty ritual and social discrimination.

questions.subject: Karnataka History
questions.question: What social practices did many Vachanakaras criticise?

options.A: Caste-based hierarchy, untouchability, ritualism without ethical substance, hypocrisy and discrimination against women and disadvantaged communities
options.B: The use of Kannada in worship

questions.explanation: Many Vachanakaras criticised caste-based hierarchy, untouchability, ritualism without ethical substance, hypocrisy and discrimination against women and disadvantaged communities.

questions.subject: Karnataka History
questions.question: What is Kayaka?

options.A: The principle of honest work and dignity of labour; work performed sincerely is treated as a form of worship
options.B: The principle of sharing resources with the community
options.C: The personal emblem of Shiva worn by a devotee

questions.explanation: Kayaka is the principle of honest work and dignity of labour; work performed sincerely is treated as a form of worship.

questions.subject: Karnataka History
questions.question: What is Dasoha?

options.A: The principle of honest work and dignity of labour
options.B: The principle of sharing the fruits of one's labour and resources for the welfare of others and the community
options.C: The practice of ritual bathing in sacred rivers

questions.explanation: Dasoha is the principle of sharing the fruits of one's labour and resources for the welfare of others and the community.

questions.subject: Karnataka History
questions.question: What is the Ishtalinga?

options.A: A temple dedicated to Shiva
options.B: The personal emblem of Shiva worn and worshipped by a Lingayat devotee; it represents direct personal devotion without dependence on an intermediary priest for personal worship
options.C: A sacred text of the Lingayat tradition

questions.explanation: Ishtalinga is the personal emblem of Shiva worn and worshipped by a Lingayat devotee; it represents direct personal devotion without dependence on an intermediary priest for personal worship.

questions.subject: Karnataka History
questions.question: What is Anubhava Mantapa?

options.A: A temple dedicated to Vishnu
options.B: An assembly or forum at Kalyana where Sharanas discussed spiritual, ethical and social questions

questions.explanation: Anubhava Mantapa is traditionally described as an assembly or forum at Kalyana where Sharanas discussed spiritual, ethical and social questions.

questions.subject: Karnataka History
questions.question: Who is traditionally associated with presiding over Anubhava Mantapa?

options.A: Basavanna

questions.explanation: Allama Prabhu is traditionally regarded as the spiritual presiding figure of Anubhava Mantapa.

questions.subject: Karnataka History
questions.question: Is the historical structure and exact institutional form of Anubhava Mantapa fully settled?

options.A: Yes, historians agree on its exact form
options.B: No, it is central to Lingayat tradition, but historians debate the precise nature, scale and documentary history of the institution as described in later accounts
options.C: It is a modern invention with no historical basis

questions.explanation: No. It is central to Lingayat tradition, but historians debate the precise nature, scale and documentary history of the institution as described in later accounts.

questions.subject: Karnataka History
questions.question: What is the importance of women in the Vachana movement?

options.A: Women were not allowed to participate
options.B: Women Sharanes composed vachanas and participated in spiritual debate, challenging restrictions on women's religious and intellectual participation

questions.explanation: Women Sharanes composed vachanas and participated in spiritual debate, challenging restrictions on women's religious and intellectual participation.

questions.subject: Karnataka History
questions.question: Name important women Vachanakaras.

options.A: Akka Mahadevi, Neelambike, Gangambike, Aydakki Lakkamma, Satyakka and other Sharanes
options.D: Purandara Dasa, Kanaka Dasa and Vijaya Dasa

questions.explanation: Important women Vachanakaras include Akka Mahadevi, Neelambike, Gangambike, Aydakki Lakkamma, Satyakka and other Sharanes.

questions.subject: Karnataka History
questions.question: What is the importance of the Vachana movement in Kannada history?

options.A: It strengthened Kannada as a medium of spiritual and philosophical expression and connected literary creativity with ethical and social reform
options.B: It replaced Kannada with Sanskrit in religious literature
options.C: It led to the decline of Kannada literature
options.D: It was limited to the royal court

questions.explanation: It strengthened Kannada as a medium of spiritual and philosophical expression and connected literary creativity with ethical and social reform.

questions.subject: Karnataka History
questions.question: What is the ankita in a vachana?

options.A: The opening invocation
options.B: The poet's devotional signature, usually a chosen name of the deity, used at the end of the vachana
options.C: The rhythmic metre of the poem

questions.explanation: Ankita is the poet's devotional signature, usually a chosen name of the deity, used at the end of the vachana.

questions.subject: Karnataka History
questions.question: What is the difference between a vachana and a conventional metrical poem?

options.A: A vachana uses a fixed classical metre, while a conventional poem does not
options.B: A vachana generally uses a flexible prose-poetic structure and conversational expression rather than depending on a fixed classical metre
options.C: A vachana is always longer than a conventional poem

questions.explanation: A vachana generally uses a flexible prose-poetic structure and conversational expression rather than depending on a fixed classical metre.

questions.subject: Karnataka History
questions.question: What is Lingayatism?

options.A: A Vaishnava tradition centred on Vishnu
options.B: A Shaiva religious tradition whose followers centre their devotion on Shiva, especially through the personal Ishtalinga

questions.explanation: Lingayatism is a Shaiva religious tradition whose followers centre their devotion on Shiva, especially through the personal Ishtalinga.

questions.subject: Karnataka History
questions.question: Who is the most prominent historical leader associated with the 12th-century Lingayat movement?

options.A: Madhvacharya
options.B: Basavanna (Basaveshwara), a minister and religious-social reformer associated with Kalyana

questions.explanation: Basavanna (Basaveshwara), a minister and religious-social reformer associated with Kalyana, is the most prominent historical leader associated with the 12th-century Lingayat movement.

questions.subject: Karnataka History
questions.question: When did the Lingayat movement associated with Basavanna become prominent?

options.A: In the 8th century CE during the Rashtrakuta period
options.B: In the 12th century CE, during the reign of the Kalachuri ruler Bijjala II at Kalyana
options.C: In the 16th century CE during the Vijayanagara period
options.D: In the 19th century CE during British rule

questions.explanation: The Lingayat movement associated with Basavanna became prominent in the 12th century CE, during the reign of the Kalachuri ruler Bijjala II at Kalyana.

questions.subject: Karnataka History
questions.question: Who was Bijjala II?

options.A: A Kalachuri ruler under whose political authority Basavanna served as a minister at Kalyana

questions.explanation: Bijjala II was a Kalachuri ruler under whose political authority Basavanna served as a minister at Kalyana.

questions.subject: Karnataka History
questions.question: What is the relationship between the Vachana movement and Lingayat tradition?

options.A: They are unrelated
options.B: The 12th-century Vachana movement was a formative spiritual and literary current closely associated with the development of the Lingayat community and its teachings
options.C: The Vachana movement was a Vaishnava movement
options.D: The Lingayat tradition predates the Vachana movement by centuries

questions.explanation: The 12th-century Vachana movement was a formative spiritual and literary current closely associated with the development of the Lingayat community and its teachings.

questions.subject: Karnataka History
questions.question: What is the Ishtalinga Diksha?

options.A: The initiation in which a guru gives a devotee the personal Ishtalinga, which the devotee wears and worships
options.B: The ritual burial of the dead

questions.explanation: Ishtalinga Diksha is the initiation in which a guru gives a devotee the personal Ishtalinga, which the devotee wears and worships.

questions.subject: Karnataka History
questions.question: What are the three traditional pillars of Lingayat spiritual life?

options.A: Guru, Linga and Jangama

questions.explanation: The three traditional pillars of Lingayat spiritual life are Guru, Linga and Jangama.

questions.subject: Karnataka History
questions.question: What does Guru mean in the Lingayat tradition?

options.A: The spiritual teacher who guides the devotee towards knowledge and realisation
options.C: A realised spiritual person or itinerant teacher

questions.explanation: Guru is the spiritual teacher who guides the devotee towards knowledge and realisation.

questions.subject: Karnataka History
questions.question: What does Linga mean in the Lingayat tradition?

options.A: The spiritual teacher
options.B: Shiva, worshipped personally through the Ishtalinga

questions.explanation: Linga refers to Shiva, worshipped personally through the Ishtalinga.

questions.subject: Karnataka History
questions.question: What does Jangama mean?

options.A: The spiritual teacher
options.C: A realised spiritual person or itinerant religious teacher who embodies and communicates the spiritual teaching

questions.explanation: Jangama refers to a realised spiritual person or itinerant religious teacher who embodies and communicates the spiritual teaching.

questions.subject: Karnataka History
questions.question: What is Shatsthala?

options.A: The eight protective spiritual disciplines
options.B: A six-stage spiritual framework in the Lingayat tradition describing the devotee's progression towards union or realisation of Shiva
options.C: The five modes of religious conduct
options.D: The three pillars of Lingayat spiritual life

questions.explanation: Shatsthala is a six-stage spiritual framework in the Lingayat tradition describing the devotee's progression towards union or realisation of Shiva.

questions.subject: Karnataka History
questions.question: What is Ashtavarana?

options.A: The eight protective spiritual disciplines or supports traditionally identified in Lingayat teaching: Guru, Linga, Jangama, Padodaka, Prasada, Vibhuti, Rudraksha and Mantra
options.B: The five modes of religious conduct
options.D: The three pillars of Lingayat spiritual life

questions.explanation: Ashtavarana means the eight protective spiritual disciplines or supports traditionally identified in Lingayat teaching: Guru, Linga, Jangama, Padodaka, Prasada, Vibhuti, Rudraksha and Mantra.

questions.subject: Karnataka History
questions.question: What is Lingachara?

options.A: Conduct centred on devotion to and worship of the Linga
options.B: Righteous and ethical conduct in everyday life
options.D: Conduct associated with the community of Shiva's devotees

questions.explanation: Lingachara is conduct centred on devotion to and worship of the Linga.

questions.subject: Karnataka History
questions.question: What is Sadachara?

options.A: Conduct centred on devotion to the Linga
options.B: Righteous and ethical conduct in everyday life

questions.explanation: Sadachara is righteous and ethical conduct in everyday life.

questions.subject: Karnataka History
questions.question: What is Shivachara?

options.A: Conduct centred on devotion to the Linga
options.B: Righteous and ethical conduct in everyday life
options.C: Conduct expressing reverence for Shiva and respect for devotees

questions.explanation: Shivachara is conduct expressing reverence for Shiva and respect for devotees.

questions.subject: Karnataka History
questions.question: What is Ganachara?

options.A: Conduct centred on devotion to the Linga
options.B: Righteous and ethical conduct in everyday life
options.C: Conduct associated with commitment to the community of Shiva's devotees and defence of its religious principles

questions.explanation: Ganachara is conduct associated with commitment to the community of Shiva's devotees and defence of its religious principles.

questions.subject: Karnataka History
questions.question: What is Bhrityachara?

options.A: Conduct centred on devotion to the Linga
options.B: Righteous and ethical conduct in everyday life
options.C: Conduct associated with the community of Shiva's devotees
options.D: Humility and service, living as a servant of Shiva and the spiritual community

questions.explanation: Bhrityachara is humility and service, living as a servant of Shiva and the spiritual community.

questions.subject: Karnataka History
questions.question: What is the traditional Lingayat practice regarding the dead?

options.A: Cremation is universally practised
options.B: Burial (samadhi) is traditionally practised in many Lingayat communities rather than cremation; practices can vary by community and circumstance
options.C: The dead are immersed in rivers
options.D: The dead are left in towers for birds

questions.explanation: Burial (samadhi) is traditionally practised in many Lingayat communities rather than cremation; practices can vary by community and circumstance.

questions.subject: Karnataka History
questions.question: What is the difference between Lingayat and Veerashaiva?

options.A: They are completely unrelated traditions
options.B: The terms are closely related and are sometimes used interchangeably, but their historical, doctrinal and community meanings are debated

questions.explanation: The terms are closely related and are sometimes used interchangeably, but their historical, doctrinal and community meanings are debated. Some Lingayat groups identify as a distinct tradition rooted in Basavanna's teachings, while Veerashaiva groups emphasise a broader Shaiva lineage and shared identity.

questions.subject: Karnataka History
questions.question: Should Lingayatism be described simply as a movement founded from nothing by Basavanna?

options.A: Yes, Basavanna created it entirely from nothing
options.B: No, Basavanna was a decisive 12th-century reformer and organiser, but Shaiva and Veerashaiva traditions and earlier lineages existed before him; the exact historical relationship is debated
options.C: Yes, it has no connection to earlier Shaiva traditions
options.D: No, it was founded by Madhvacharya

questions.explanation: No. Basavanna was a decisive 12th-century reformer and organiser, but Shaiva and Veerashaiva traditions and earlier lineages existed before him; the exact historical relationship is debated.

questions.subject: Karnataka History
questions.question: What is the importance of the Lingayat movement in Karnataka?

options.A: It shaped Karnataka's religious identity, Kannada devotional literature, social thought, community institutions and traditions of education and service
options.B: It led to the decline of Kannada literature
options.C: It was limited to the royal family

questions.explanation: It shaped Karnataka's religious identity, Kannada devotional literature, social thought, community institutions and traditions of education and service.

questions.subject: Karnataka History
questions.question: What are Lingayat maths?

options.A: Religious and educational institutions led by pontiffs or swamis that preserve teachings, conduct religious activities and often support education and social service

questions.explanation: Mathas are religious and educational institutions led by pontiffs or swamis that preserve teachings, conduct religious activities and often support education and social service.

questions.subject: Karnataka History
questions.question: Who was Basavanna?

options.A: A 12th-century philosopher, minister, social reformer and Vachana poet who advocated devotion, Kayaka, Dasoha and ethical equality
options.B: A 13th-century philosopher who founded Dvaita Vedanta

questions.explanation: Basavanna was a 12th-century philosopher, minister, social reformer and Vachana poet who advocated devotion, Kayaka, Dasoha and ethical equality.

questions.subject: Karnataka History
questions.question: What was Basavanna's ankita?

options.A: Gudeshwara

questions.explanation: Basavanna's ankita was Kudalasangamadeva.

questions.subject: Karnataka History
questions.question: Where is Kudalasangama?

options.A: A pilgrimage centre in present-day Bagalkot district, Karnataka, associated with the confluence of the Krishna and Malaprabha rivers and with Basavanna
options.B: A pilgrimage centre in Hassan district
options.D: A Jain centre in Dakshina Kannada

questions.explanation: Kudalasangama is a pilgrimage centre in present-day Bagalkot district, Karnataka, associated with the confluence of the Krishna and Malaprabha rivers and with Basavanna.

questions.subject: Karnataka History
questions.question: Who was Allama Prabhu?

options.A: A 12th-century mystic, philosopher and Vachana poet known for profound spiritual and non-dual expression

questions.explanation: Allama Prabhu was a 12th-century mystic, philosopher and Vachana poet known for profound spiritual and non-dual expression.

questions.subject: Karnataka History
questions.question: What was Allama Prabhu's ankita?

options.A: Kudalasangamadeva

questions.explanation: Allama Prabhu's ankita was Gudeshwara (Guheshwara).

questions.subject: Karnataka History
questions.question: Who was Akka Mahadevi?

options.A: A 12th-century woman mystic and Vachana poet whose devotion was directed to Channamallikarjuna

questions.explanation: Akka Mahadevi was a 12th-century woman mystic and Vachana poet whose devotion was directed to Channamallikarjuna.

questions.subject: Karnataka History
questions.question: What was Akka Mahadevi's ankita?

options.A: Kudalasangamadeva

questions.explanation: Akka Mahadevi's ankita was Channamallikarjuna.

questions.subject: Karnataka History
questions.question: Which place is associated with Akka Mahadevi's spiritual journey?

options.A: Srisailam is strongly associated with her later spiritual life in traditional accounts

questions.explanation: Srisailam is strongly associated with Akka Mahadevi's later spiritual life in traditional accounts.

questions.subject: Karnataka History
questions.question: Who was Channabasavanna?

options.A: A major Sharana thinker and Vachana composer, traditionally identified as Basavanna's nephew

questions.explanation: Channabasavanna was a major Sharana thinker and Vachana composer, traditionally identified as Basavanna's nephew.

questions.subject: Karnataka History
questions.question: What was Channabasavanna's ankita?

options.A: Kudalasangamadeva

questions.explanation: Channabasavanna's ankita was Kudalachannasangama.

questions.subject: Karnataka History
questions.question: Who was Siddharama of Sonnalige?

options.A: A 12th-century Sharana saint and Vachana poet associated with Sonnalige, identified with present-day Solapur

questions.explanation: Siddharama was a 12th-century Sharana saint and Vachana poet associated with Sonnalige, identified with present-day Solapur.

questions.subject: Karnataka History
questions.question: What was Siddharama's ankita?

options.A: Kudalasangamadeva

questions.explanation: Siddharama's ankita was Kapilasadhammallikarjuna (also written Kapilasiddhamallikarjuna).

questions.subject: Karnataka History
questions.question: Who was Jedara Dasimayya?

options.A: An early Vachana poet traditionally regarded as one of the earliest Sharanas

questions.explanation: Jedara Dasimayya was an early Vachana poet traditionally regarded as one of the earliest Sharanas.

questions.subject: Karnataka History
questions.question: What was Jedara Dasimayya's ankita?

options.A: Kudalasangamadeva

questions.explanation: Jedara Dasimayya's ankita was Ramanatha.

questions.subject: Karnataka History
questions.question: Who was Ambigara Chowdaiah?

options.A: A Vachana poet associated with the boatman community and known for direct criticism of hypocrisy and social injustice

questions.explanation: Ambigara Chowdaiah was a Vachana poet associated with the boatman community and known for direct criticism of hypocrisy and social injustice.

questions.subject: Karnataka History
questions.question: What was Ambigara Chowdaiah's ankita?

options.A: Kudalasangamadeva

questions.explanation: Ambigara Chowdaiah's ankita was Prabhudeva.

questions.subject: Karnataka History
questions.question: Who was Madara Chennaiah?

options.A: An early Sharana poet traditionally associated with the leather-working community and remembered for his devotional and egalitarian outlook

questions.explanation: Madara Chennaiah was an early Sharana poet traditionally associated with the leather-working community and remembered for his devotional and egalitarian outlook.

questions.subject: Karnataka History
questions.question: Who was Madivala Machideva?

options.A: A Sharana and Vachana poet traditionally associated with the washerman community and known for his devotion and service

questions.explanation: Madivala Machideva was a Sharana and Vachana poet traditionally associated with the washerman community and known for his devotion and service.

questions.subject: Karnataka History
questions.question: What is the significance of the Sharanes and Sharanas?

options.A: They represent a diverse community of women and men who contributed vachanas and promoted spiritual practice and ethical reform
options.B: They were only from the Brahmin community
options.D: They opposed the use of Kannada

questions.explanation: They represent a diverse community of women and men who contributed vachanas and promoted spiritual practice and ethical reform.

questions.subject: Karnataka History
questions.question: What was the Haridasa movement?

options.A: A Kannada Vaishnava devotional movement that spread bhakti to Vishnu through songs, kirtanas and accessible compositions
options.B: A Shaiva reform movement of the 12th century

questions.explanation: The Haridasa movement was a Kannada Vaishnava devotional movement that spread bhakti to Vishnu through songs, kirtanas and accessible compositions.

questions.subject: Karnataka History
questions.question: What does the word Haridasa mean?

options.A: Servant or devotee of Hari, a name of Vishnu

questions.explanation: Haridasa means servant or devotee of Hari, a name of Vishnu.

questions.subject: Karnataka History
questions.question: Which philosophical school strongly influenced the Haridasa movement?

options.A: Advaita Vedanta

questions.explanation: Dvaita Vedanta, established by Madhvacharya, strongly influenced the Haridasa movement.

questions.subject: Karnataka History
questions.question: Who founded Dvaita Vedanta?

options.A: Adi Shankaracharya
options.C: Madhvacharya, the 13th-century philosopher associated with Udupi

questions.explanation: Madhvacharya, the 13th-century philosopher associated with Udupi, founded Dvaita Vedanta.

questions.subject: Karnataka History
questions.question: What is the central idea of Dvaita philosophy?

options.A: It teaches the ultimate non-difference of Atman and Brahman
options.B: It teaches a real distinction between God, individual souls and matter, and holds Vishnu to be the supreme reality
options.C: It teaches that individual souls and the universe are real and exist in dependence on Brahman
options.D: It denies the existence of God

questions.explanation: Dvaita philosophy teaches a real distinction between God, individual souls and matter, and holds Vishnu to be the supreme reality.

questions.subject: Karnataka History
questions.question: When did the Haridasa movement become especially influential?

options.A: During the 8th century CE
options.C: It flourished particularly during the Vijayanagara period, especially from the 15th and 16th centuries onward, while its roots are earlier

questions.explanation: It flourished particularly during the Vijayanagara period, especially from the 15th and 16th centuries onward, while its roots are earlier.

questions.subject: Karnataka History
questions.question: What is Dasa Sahitya?

options.A: The devotional literature composed by Haridasas, mainly in Kannada
options.B: The Vachana literature of the Sharanas

questions.explanation: Dasa Sahitya is the devotional literature composed by Haridasas, mainly in Kannada.

questions.subject: Karnataka History
questions.question: What are Devaranamas?

options.A: Devotional songs in praise of God, especially Vishnu and his forms
